q: Which Romanesque baptistery is known for its eight monolithic columns alternating with four pillars and significant vertical height?
n: The Pisa Baptistery's interior has eight monolithic columns alternating with four piers in a ring, under a tall conical dome. It is the largest baptistery in Italy. Source: Opera della Primaziale Pisana; UNESCO (Piazza del Duomo, Pisa).

q: Which church is the most important work of Renaissance architecture?
n: St. Peter's Basilica, shaped by Bramante, Michelangelo, Maderno and others, is the most important work of Renaissance architecture. Source: UNESCO (Vatican City); Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which style stresses symmetry, geometry and regularity of parts?
n: Renaissance architecture stresses symmetry, geometry and regular proportions of parts, from Brunelleschi, Alberti and Palladio. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Renaissance architecture.

q: Which architectural style adapted the classical orders of columns from the Greeks?
n: Renaissance architects revived and adapted the classical orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian, after Greek and Roman models) through Vitruvius. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Renaissance architecture; Ching.

q: Where was the birthplace of Italian Renaissance art and architecture?
n: Florence was the birthplace of Italian Renaissance art and architecture, with Brunelleschi's dome (1420–36) and Foundling Hospital. Source: UNESCO (Historic Centre of Florence).

q: Which period is called the rebirth of the classics?
n: "Renaissance" means rebirth: the revival of classical Greek and Roman art and learning from the 15th century. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Renaissance.

q: Which symmetrical villa did Andrea Palladio design?
n: Palladio's Villa Capra "La Rotonda" near Vicenza is perfectly symmetrical, with four identical porticoes around a central domed hall. Source: UNESCO (City of Vicenza and the Palladian Villas of the Veneto).

q: Which movement is described as vivid, virile, intense, free, decorative and illogical?
n: Baroque is classically described as vivid, virile, intense, free, decorative and illogical, a dramatic break from Renaissance calm. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture.

q: What defines Palladian architecture?
n: Palladian architecture is defined by harmonious proportion, from Vitruvian ratios and symmetry, as in Palladio's Four Books of Architecture. Source: Palladio, I Quattro Libri dell'Architettura; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which is a key trait of Renaissance architecture?
o: Symmetry, proportion and the classical orders
n: Renaissance architecture's key traits are symmetry, proportion and the classical orders. Pointed arches and flying buttresses are Gothic. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Renaissance architecture.

q: Which features were revived from antiquity in the Renaissance?
n: The Renaissance revived classical domes and columns (the orders), as in Brunelleschi's Florence dome and Bramante's Tempietto. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Renaissance architecture.

q: Which church is regarded as the greatest in Christendom?
n: St. Peter's Basilica, long the largest church in the world, is regarded as the greatest church in Christendom. Source: Vatican official site; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who first proposed changing St. Peter's to a Latin cross plan?
n: Bramante planned St. Peter's as a Greek cross. Raphael, his successor (1514), first proposed lengthening it into a Latin cross, which Maderno finally built. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, St. Peter's Basilica.

q: Who was the final architect responsible for completing St. Peter's Basilica?
n: Of the choices, Gian Lorenzo Bernini was the last great architect at St. Peter's. After Maderno's nave and facade (1607–15), Bernini finished the interior (baldacchino, Cathedra Petri) and designed the piazza (1656–67). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, St. Peter's Basilica; Vatican official site.

q: Who sculpted the Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica?
n: Michelangelo carved the Pietà in St. Peter's in 1498–99, his only signed work. Source: Vatican official site (St. Peter's Basilica); Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who designed the piazza in front of St. Peter's, ringed by 284 Tuscan columns?
n: Bernini designed St. Peter's Square (1656–67), embraced by two curved colonnades of 284 Tuscan columns in four rows. Source: Vatican official site; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which part of St. Peter's did Michelangelo design?
n: Michelangelo, chief architect from 1546, designed the great dome of St. Peter's. It was completed after his death by Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana (1590). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, St. Peter's Basilica.

q: What was Bramante's role at St. Peter's?
o: First architect of the new basilica
n: Donato Bramante was the first architect of the new St. Peter's. He laid the foundation stone in 1506 to a Greek-cross plan for Pope Julius II. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Donato Bramante.

q: Who designed the minor domes of St. Peter's?
n: Giacomo Barozzi da Vignola designed the minor side cupolas of St. Peter's, built later by della Porta. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Vignola; Fletcher.

q: Who designed the main façade of St. Peter's?
n: Carlo Maderno extended the nave into a Latin cross and built the main facade (1607–14). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Carlo Maderno.

q: Which is considered the first Renaissance building?
o: Loggia of the Ospedale degli Innocenti
n: Brunelleschi's loggia of the Ospedale degli Innocenti in Florence (begun 1419) is considered the first Renaissance building. Its round arches on Corinthian columns are based on modular proportion. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Filippo Brunelleschi.

q: _Whatis the tropical modernist work of Geoffrey Bawa?
n: Geoffrey Bawa's Heritance Kandalama Hotel (1994) in Sri Lanka is the icon of his tropical modernism. It is built into a rock face and overgrown with jungle. Source: Geoffrey Bawa Trust; Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
